@copilot Update this PR directly to consistently call captured gRPC request headers "headers" rather than "metadata". Main is targeting 3.0, and the user explicitly wants the public API and configuration renames included as breaking changes, without retaining the old names solely for compatibility. Do not create a separate PR.

Rename RPC_STABLE_REQUEST_METADATA_KEY_ATTRIBUTE_PREFIX to RPC_STABLE_REQUEST_HEADER_KEY_ATTRIBUTE_PREFIX; CapturedGrpcMetadataUtil and its file to CapturedGrpcRequestHeadersUtil; CapturedGrpcMetadataUtilTest and its file to CapturedGrpcRequestHeadersUtilTest; stableMetadataAttributeKey to stableHeaderAttributeKey in GrpcAttributesExtractorTest; and stableMetadataAttributePrefix to stableHeaderAttributePrefix in AbstractGrpcTest. Update all references and imports.

Rename GrpcTelemetryBuilder.setClientRequestMetadata(IncludeExclude) to setClientRequestHeaders(IncludeExclude), and setServerRequestMetadata(IncludeExclude) to setServerRequestHeaders(IncludeExclude). Remove the already-deprecated setCapturedClientRequestMetadata(List<String>) and setCapturedServerRequestMetadata(List<String>) methods rather than renaming obsolete APIs. Update their callers and affected tests.

Rename all four flat properties otel.instrumentation.grpc.{client,server}.request-metadata.{included,excluded} to otel.instrumentation.grpc.{client,server}.request-headers.{included,excluded}. Rename corresponding declarative paths java.grpc.{client,server}.request_metadata.{included,excluded} to java.grpc.{client,server}.request_headers.{included,excluded}. Wire both forms consistently, including any bridge mappings and fixtures. Rename capture-related fields, parameters, getters, and helper/test names to requestHeaders, clientRequestHeaders, serverRequestHeaders, getClientRequestHeaders(), getServerRequestHeaders(), and corresponding header terminology. Follow references through gRPC and dependent Armeria integration so all consumers are updated.

Keep Metadata terminology where it describes actual io.grpc.Metadata objects, gRPC metadata-key validation, or legacy rpc.grpc.request.metadata.* attributes. Preserve that legacy attribute prefix and the PR's rpc.request.header.* preview output, all three semconv modes, selectors, case normalization, multi-value handling, and filtering. This is a naming/API migration, not a change to capture semantics.

Update metadata.yaml, existing README settings tables, public API documentation, configuration/test fixtures, and concise breaking-change CHANGELOG entries for the API removals/renames and config migration. Keep migration history in CHANGELOG rather than READMEs. Run the narrowest applicable spotlessApply directly before relevant tests, and exercise flat/declarative configuration, capture behavior, and dependent consumers. Keep the existing PR's draft/ready state unchanged. Do not edit the PR title or description; the coordinating session will handle those after coding.

threads.body:
@copilot Update this existing PR directly to finish its gRPC request-header capture migration on current main. Do not create another PR. The user has confirmed that repository-wide documentation cleanup is being handled in a separate PR; keep this assignment limited to the existing gRPC header-capture changes and their directly affected code, tests, configuration, metadata, and existing gRPC README.

First merge the latest upstream main into this PR's existing head branch, copilot/align-grpc-headers, preserving that head as the first-parent history. Main already contains #21034, #21043, and #21045: the current RPC conventions are unconditional for 3.0, legacy/duplicate emission paths and RPC selection helpers have been removed, and the shared legacy APIs have been removed. Resolve conflicts by preserving those landed changes together with this PR's metadata-to-headers migration. Do not resurrect RPC mode selection, legacy emission, removed helpers, or redundant test executions.

Remove the obsolete Stable qualification from this PR's gRPC capture helpers, fields, constants, and test variables. Use one unqualified set of names such as RPC_REQUEST_HEADER_KEY_ATTRIBUTE_PREFIX, createLiteralRequestHeaderAttributeKeys(), requestHeaderAttributeKey(), and literalRequestHeaderAttributeKeys. Do not substitute Preview for Stable: there is only one supported RPC emission shape. Update imports and all directly affected callers.

Preserve this PR's intended API and configuration migration: setClientRequestHeaders(IncludeExclude), setServerRequestHeaders(IncludeExclude), the request-headers.included/excluded flat settings, the request_headers declarative paths, and removal of the deprecated list setters. The captured attributes should use rpc.request.header.<key> unconditionally when capture is configured, without RPC preview/dup flags or legacy rpc.grpc.request.metadata.<key> emission. Keep Metadata terminology when it names actual io.grpc.Metadata objects or protocol-specific key validation.

Adapt the touched capture tests to direct, single-mode expectations and unqualified names. Preserve selector inclusion/exclusion, case normalization, multi-value capture, ASCII-only validation, and other existing capture semantics. Do not add assertions solely to check the absence of retired attribute spellings. Update the existing gRPC README's PR-specific description so it describes current header capture without obsolete RPC preview/dup instructions. Keep existing API/configuration migration documentation accurate, but do not perform repository-wide documentation, generated-catalog, or knowledge-article cleanup.

Run the narrowest applicable spotlessApply directly before relevant tests, and validate the affected gRPC library/javaagent and configuration behavior plus directly affected dependent consumers where applicable. Preserve this PR's draft state.

replies.body: Merged latest main into the existing branch and aligned capture with the unconditional `rpc.request.header.<key>` convention. Removed Stable/legacy capture paths, updated direct tests and README, and validated the gRPC library/javaagent, Armeria integration, and declarative config mapping. Commit: `2398e931`.

threads.body: [Config] The existing Unreleased gRPC migration entry at lines 260–263 still recommends `otel.instrumentation.grpc.{client,server}.request-metadata.included`. After this rename, `GrpcConfig` no longer reads those properties, so following that migration silently disables header capture. Please update or consolidate that entry so it points directly to `request-headers.included`.
